title: Roll branch-per-bead out to consuming repos (chem, einstein, ...)
description: After verified-sandbox-rbz, each consuming repo must, before its next sandbox run: (1) run 'uv run sandbox install-hooks' (sandbox run now refuses a v1 guard); (2) start from a clean tree on the base branch (run refuses a dirty tree); (3) update sandbox-prompt.md git-policy section, which still says 'Do not commit' -- the loop appends an overriding policy, but the contradiction should go. Also update the new-verified-repo skill's prompt template the same way. chem has a loop running from before the change (old inode); do this after it drains.

title: Branch-per-bead commits: workers commit to sandbox/<bead-id>, never main
description:
Workers are currently forbidden to commit at all: the pre-commit/pre-push hooks installed by __init__.py refuse whenever BEADS_ACTOR=sandbox, and the worker prompt says leave the tree dirty. Every bead in a run therefore lands in one shared dirty tree. Observed in einstein on 2026-09-29: six beads' work (tix, b3b, zfp, 9it, uts, n7n) interleaved in the same files and had to be committed as one commit. You can't review, revert, or bisect them one bead at a time. A shared dirty tree also blocks parallel workers (a worktree per worker needs a branch to hold its output).

Change: before dispatch, the loop checks out (or creates) sandbox/<bead-id> from main. The worker commits its work plus its handoff file on that branch. After the worker exits, the loop returns the host to main (or the worktree is discarded) and moves on. The pre-commit hook refuses only when BEADS_ACTOR=sandbox AND the current branch is not sandbox/*. Keep pre-push refusing for sandbox workers; the host/human pushes. Workers never merge. Merging stays with the human or an independent checker (producer/checker separation). Update the worker prompt's git policy to match.

Open question: with a single shared checkout, the loop must handle a worker that leaves uncommitted changes (e.g. auto-commit them as a WIP commit on the bead branch, or refuse to switch). Decide and document.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A worker commit on main (or any non-sandbox/* branch) with BEADS_ACTOR=sandbox is refused; on sandbox/<id> it succeeds. Tests for both, and each must fail before the hook change. 2) Pushes by sandbox workers are still refused. 3) A two-bead run produces two branches, each containing only its bead's diff and handoff, with main unchanged. Verified by an integration test or a recorded dry run. 4) Leftover uncommitted worker changes are never silently dropped or carried onto the next bead's branch. 5) README and worker prompt git-policy text updated; host-side commits unaffected.
close_reason: Implemented: sandbox/<id> branch per bead (incl. triage), v2 pre-commit guard (sandbox commits only on sandbox/?*), pre-push still refuses, host WIP-commits leftovers onto the bead branch, run stops if HEAD left elsewhere or any non-sandbox/ branch moves, refuses dirty/detached/sandbox-branch start; install-hooks upgrades v1 in place, check_hooks rejects v1. Also fixed pre-existing: git refused /workspace in-container (dubious ownership) -> safe.directory via GIT_CONFIG_* env; workers get sandbox git identity. 32 tests pass; each new test mutation-checked to fail; commit/refusal verified inside real claude-chem image.

title: Shared bead queue across machines: dolt pull before dispatch, claim-and-push
description:
Today the loop reads and writes only the local embedded Dolt DB. A second consumer on another machine -- a Claude Code cloud session, or a loop on another laptop -- pulls its own copy from the Dolt remote (refs/dolt/data on the git remote, e.g. chem's sync.remote) and neither side sees the other's claims until someone runs bd dolt push/pull by hand. Result: the same bead dispatched twice, and conflicting pushes. Workaround today: partition by hand via [tool.sandbox] park.

Proposal (opt-in, e.g. [tool.sandbox] shared-queue = true):
- bd dolt pull before each selection (next_ready / next_stale), under the bdlock so it cannot race worker bd calls.
- The LOOP claims the bead (bd update --claim) and bd dolt push-es before starting the worker; if the push is rejected (someone else pushed first), pull, re-check the bead is still unclaimed by another actor, and pick again. The worker's own --claim becomes a no-op.
- bd dolt push after each worker finishes, so closes/notes are visible remotely.
- Distinguish claimants: BEADS_ACTOR per machine (sandbox@<host>) so a stale claim from another machine is not re-dispatched as 'stale' locally while that machine is still working it -- needs a lease/heartbeat or a staleness age, since in_progress alone cannot say whether the other side is alive.

Open questions:
- Dolt merge semantics for concurrent edits to the same issue row: does bd dolt pull auto-merge or conflict? Must test with two real clones.
- Auth: the remote is git+ssh://; cloud sessions may only have HTTPS GitHub access.
- Cost: a pull/push per dispatch is network round-trips on every loop iteration; parallel mode (max-parallel>1) multiplies it.
- A cloud session is not the loop: document the protocol it must follow (pull, claim, push before work; push after) in the prompt or a small script.
acceptance_criteria: With shared-queue enabled, two loops on two clones of the same repo (same Dolt remote) never run the same bead concurrently: a test with two real clones racing to claim shows exactly one winner per bead and the loser picks another; claims and closes from one side are visible to the other within one dispatch; a push rejection is retried, not treated as a failed bead; shared-queue off leaves today's behaviour and all existing tests passing; the stale-claim rule does not re-dispatch a bead another machine claimed within the lease window.
close_reason: Shipped: claims.py (refs/claims/<id> on the git remote) + Dolt pull/push in both loops, opt-in via shared-queue. Evidence: 6-way claim race 1 winner (test + 5 manual rounds); two real loops on two clones drain 6 beads with each run exactly once, both sequential and max-parallel=2; a bead held by another machine is not dispatched; live/expired lease and CAS release tested; mutants (no claim / ignore held claims) fail tests. Real bd: disjoint edits merge, same-issue edits abort pull -- VS_BD_TESTS=1. Not covered: a real Claude worker on real bd end to end; no heartbeat, so a bead outliving claim-lease-hours can be taken over.

title: Parallel workers within one repo via per-bead git worktrees
description:
Today one loop per repo runs beads sequentially: loop.sh takes a repo-wide .sandbox.lock and checks out sandbox/<bead-id> in the single working tree, so a second loop in the same repo is refused. Swarming means starting a loop per repo by hand.

Proposal: a max-parallel knob in [tool.sandbox] (default 1 = today's behaviour). Each concurrent worker gets its own git worktree (e.g. .sandbox-worktrees/<bead-id>) on sandbox/<bead-id>, bind-mounted as /workspace; the lock moves from per-repo to per-bead (bd claim is the natural one). The host tree is never checked out underneath the user.

Open questions:
- Conflicting beads: two workers editing the same files merge-conflict at review time. Options: dispatch only beads bd ready says are independent, a per-bead 'touches' hint, or accept conflicts and leave them to the human merge.
- .beads/ Dolt DB is shared across worktrees -- concurrent bd writes from N containers need checking (embedded Dolt locking).
- uv venv: UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/venv is per-container already; the shared uv cache volume is fine.
- Rate limits: all workers share one CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and the :4000 proxy; the fast-failure backoff must not make N workers retry in lockstep.
- Dirty-tree check and WIP commit logic must run per worktree, not on the host tree.
acceptance_criteria: max-parallel=N runs up to N workers concurrently in one repo, each in its own worktree on sandbox/<bead-id>; the host working tree's branch never changes during a run; max-parallel=1 behaves exactly as today (existing tests pass); a test covers two concurrent beads producing two branches with no cross-contamination; concurrent bd updates from workers verified not to corrupt or lose issue state.
close_reason: Shipped in 28e9d51: max-parallel=N, one worktree per bead. Evidence: 11 new tests (tests/test_parallel.py) incl. overlap proven by a two-worker handshake, host HEAD recorded as main during the run, no double dispatch, ref-move stop, fast-fail/park parity; mutation-checked (each of 4 mutants fails >=1 test). max-parallel=1 unchanged: all 32 prior tests pass. Real docker e2e with a fake-worker image: 3 concurrent containers claimed/committed/closed via the shared DB; Ctrl-C at 1/3/7s left no containers, worktrees or locks. bd concurrency: unlocked 47/60 container creates failed with embedded-Dolt panics (some 'failed' writes landed); behind bdlock/bd 60/60, and the opt-in VS_DOCKER_TESTS test passes. Open by design: same-file conflicts surface at merge; shared OAuth rate limit.
